title: Ships and Navigation
objective: After this level you can explain how new ships and tools let Europeans sail farther.
summary: Portugal's caravels, with triangular sails that could beat against the wind, carried explorers down Africa's coast: to the Cape of Good Hope in 1488 and India in 1498.

cards.headline: “Henry the Navigator” never went on a voyage of exploration.
cards.body: Portugal’s Prince Henry paid for them instead. His captains needed a ship that could probe an unknown coast and still get home. What did they build?

cards.headline: A ship that sails into the wind
cards.body: The Portuguese developed the caravel to explore Africa’s coast: a light ship with two or three masts and triangular lateen sails. Its great advantage was that it could sail against the wind, zig-zagging forward. On a coast where the wind kept blowing the wrong way, that was the difference between exploring and being stuck. Out of sight of land, sailors trusted a compass, known to European mariners since the 12th century.

cards.headline: Gold, and people
cards.body: Why keep sailing south? Henry wanted a share of West Africa’s trade, especially in gold and in enslaved people. In 1441 a caravel came home with both, and the costly voyages suddenly paid. It’s an uncomfortable fact worth keeping: from the start, these voyages traded in human beings.

events.label: A caravel brings gold dust and enslaved Africans to Portugal
Prince Henry dies; the voyages go on
Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape of Good Hope
Vasco da Gama reaches Calicut in India

learned: Prince Henry sponsored voyages but never sailed on them
Caravels could sail against the wind

questions.prompt: What gave the Portuguese caravel its big advantage for exploring?

options.label: Rows of oars for calm days
A huge hold for cannon and cargo
Triangular sails that let it sail against the wind
An iron hull that resisted storms
options.rationale: It was a light wooden ship.

questions.explanation: The caravel’s lateen (triangular) sails let it sail against the wind.

questions.prompt: Why did Prince Henry pay for voyages down Africa’s west coast?

options.label: To prove the Earth was round
To share in West Africa’s trade in gold and enslaved people
To find new lands for Portuguese farmers
To map the coast for the Pope

questions.explanation: Henry wanted part of West Africa’s trade, especially gold and enslaved people; a caravel returned with both in 1441.

questions.prompt: Sailing on from Henry’s voyages, who first reached India by rounding Africa?

options.label: Bartolomeu Dias, in 1488
options.rationale: Dias rounded the Cape but turned back.

options.label: Prince Henry, in 1441
options.rationale: Henry never sailed on these voyages.

options.label: Christopher Columbus, in 1492
options.rationale: He sailed west, not around Africa.

questions.explanation: Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488; da Gama sailed on to Calicut, India, in 1498.
